terms.grammar: noun phrase: scida, scidae f., with the genitive persōnae
terms.comment: Levi and Bini’s phrase; Traupman and Morgan–Owens have none. Scida (scheda) is classically a strip of papyrus or a sheet of paper (Lewis & Short). The Romans carried no identity papers; the nearest thing was the tessera hospitālis, the token whose matching halves let guest-friends know each other (Plautus, Poenulus; Lewis & Short, s.v. tessera).

terms.grammar: noun phrase: scida with the adjective cīvīlis
noun phrase: scida with the adjective cīvica

phrases.english: Show your identity card to the customs officer.

sources: Lewis & Short: scida · Lewis & Short: persona · Lewis & Short: civilis · Lewis & Short: civicus · Lewis & Short: tessera
